corrections.source_says: The source does not explicitly define which prompt pairs enter the mean or how similarities are aggregated. It says prompts in the Expandora condition had lower average semantic similarity, and names a paired t-test for usage logs. Within-person computation is plausible but unconfirmed; remove the categorical claim that it compares only one person's prompts and excludes across-person comparisons, and record the missing comparison-set/aggregation details as unknown. The resulting flexibility/with_ai classification and participant unit should be flagged as uncertain rather than presented as source-confirmed.
corrections.quote: By analyzing what prompts users used to generate images, it was shown that prompts in the Expandora condition were more diverse with lower average semantic similarity between prompts

confirmed: Source version is arXiv:2503.00791v1 dated 2 Mar 2025, carrying the CHI EA 2025 copyright block and DOI 10.1145/3706599.3720189; the supplied PDF has 10 pages. The full markdown and all PDF pages, including Appendices A-D, were read (PDF pp. 1-10; version stamp on p. 1).
The title and author list DaEun Choi, Kihoon Son, Hyunjoon Jung, and Juho Kim match the document (PDF pp. 1-2, title/author block and ACM reference).

The evaluation reports eight people, with the same participants completing both conditions; the arm counts of eight must not be summed into sixteen people. No randomized count or exclusions are reported, so n_randomized=null remains appropriate (PDF p. 4, Section 5; p. 5, procedure; p. 9, Table 1).

The paper says system and topic order was counterbalanced, without stating random allocation of participants or condition order. No randomized people study is established by either study; retaining assignment.randomized='not_stated', design_class='other', and context_class='none' for the incompletely specified small evaluation is supported (PDF pp. 2-3, Section 3; pp. 4-5, Section 5).

Expandora uses GPT-4o for prompt suggestions and DALL-E 2 for image generation, offering four prompt suggestions; the comparator is ChatGPT with image generation (PDF p. 3, Section 4.1.2; p. 4, Sections 4.2 and 5).
Each of the two mascot-design tasks lasted 25 minutes, preceded by a 5-minute tutorial; the interview after both sessions lasted 15 minutes (PDF p. 5, Section 5 continuation).

S1-O2 reported values match exactly: Expandora prompt count M=30.88, SD=9.16; baseline M=14, SD=4.72; p=0.0007. These are prompt-count means for the eight-person evaluation, not participant counts (PDF p. 5, Section 6.1; N=8 on p. 4, Section 5).

S1-O1 reported values match exactly: Expandora average semantic similarity M=0.476, SD=0.10; baseline M=0.666, SD=0.10; p=0.0032. The authors describe lower similarity as more diverse prompts (PDF p. 5, Section 6.2).
The usage-log test is described as a two-sample paired t-test; survey data use a Wilcoxon signed-rank test and a 7-point Likert scale (PDF p. 5, Section 6).

S1-O3 reported values match Table 2: aggregated CSI baseline M=5.06, STD=0.81; Expandora M=5.53, STD=0.80; P=0.383. This is a survey measure, correctly marked self_report and not scored_on_output (PDF p. 5, Sections 6 and 6.2; p. 9, Table 2).
Every number in the one_line_finding is reproduced in Section 6.1, Section 6.2, or Table 2; the CSI result supports no statistically significant difference (PDF pp. 4-5 and p. 9, Table 2).

The evaluation is below the 50-person eligibility threshold; core=no and criterion_2_at_least_50_people=not_met remain supported. The paper does not provide an image-creativity rating or a clearly defined across-person diversity analysis; Appendix D presents image examples (PDF p. 4, Section 5; p. 5, Section 6.2; p. 8, Appendix D; p. 10, Figure 3).
This is an empirical system paper with a formative study and a comparative evaluation, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates to extract (PDF pp. 2-6, Sections 3-8).
summary: The eight-person comparison and all three reported outcome-statistic strings match the PDF, but random assignment is not stated. Corrections cover the omitted formative study and included appendices, Adobe affiliation, conflicting sex counts, and unsupported specificity in the prompt-similarity method.
